QuestionStmt.S: The assets of a person reduced in his business such that the rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of the existing assets. If the assets were initially ₹ 10 lakhs and due to loss they reduce to ₹ 10000 after 3 years, then the number of years required for the person to be bankrupt will be

Solution.S:
Step 1: Let the assets be x at time t. Since the rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of the existing assets, we have:

$$\frac{dx}{dt} = -k\sqrt{x}$$

Step 2: Separate the variables:

$$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = -k \, dt$$

Step 3: Integrate both sides:

$$2\sqrt{x} = -kt + C$$

Step 4: Initially, at t = 0, x = 10,00,000 (10 lakhs).

$$2\sqrt{10,00,000} = C \Rightarrow C = 2000$$

So, $2\sqrt{x} = -kt + 2000$.

Step 5: After 3 years, x = 10,000:

$$2\sqrt{10,000} = -3k + 2000$$

$$200 = -3k + 2000 \Rightarrow k = 600$$

Thus, $2\sqrt{x} = -600t + 2000$.

Step 6: Bankruptcy occurs when x = 0. Let T be the time to bankruptcy:

$$0 = -600T + 2000$$

$$T = \frac{2000}{600} = \frac{10}{3} \text{ years}$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\frac{10}{3} \text{ years}}$$
